title: Week 7 Assessment: Negotiation, Teams and Finance
intro: This assessment deepens what you have practised: negotiating, resolving team conflict, leading change and thinking about money and evidence. Part A is auto-graded from lessons you completed. Part B has a decision scenario, a conflict role-play and a written task.

items.prompt: A social media post promises "guaranteed 30% monthly returns" from a new investment scheme and says it is limited to the first 50 people. What is the best response?

options.feedback: False urgency and guaranteed returns are warning signs.

options.text: Treat it as a likely scam, check regulator registration and avoid sending any money.
options.feedback: Guaranteed high returns and pressure are classic red flags.

options.text: Invest a small amount to test it.
options.feedback: Even a small amount can be lost and may lead to more demands.

options.text: Share it with friends to help them.

items.why: No legitimate investment can guarantee extreme returns, and urgency is a warning sign.

items.setup: Two team members both want to present the final demo to the client. You are the project lead and need to resolve it fairly.

turns.they: I should present. I did most of the work!

options.feedback: Giving in without discussion ignores the other person.

options.text: Let us each say why this matters to us. What do you want from presenting?
options.feedback: It looks for interests behind positions.
options.reply: I want to show my module to the client.

turns.they: I want to present because my part is the most visible to the client.

options.feedback: Judging does not solve the problem.

options.text: So each of you wants your module shown. Could each present your part for five minutes, with one of you opening and the other closing?
options.feedback: It creates an option that meets both interests.
A coin toss ignores interests but is quick.

turns.they: That works, but who will decide the order?

options.text: I do not care, decide yourselves.
options.feedback: Avoiding the decision invites a new dispute.

options.text: I will propose the order based on the demo flow and send it in writing, and we review it after the client call.
options.feedback: A clear agreement that is written and reviewed.

items.why: Find interests, create options and agree in writing with a review.

items.prompt: Write 100 to 130 words: a simple monthly budget plan for a first-job salary of Rs 30,000 (you decide the categories and amounts), including one saving goal and one item you would negotiate or reduce.

descriptors.3: Categories with amounts that add up.

items.modelAnswer: Rent and food Rs 12,000; transport Rs 3,000; phone and internet Rs 1,000; learning Rs 2,000; family Rs 4,000; emergency fund Rs 4,000; personal Rs 3,000; buffer Rs 1,000. Goal: build an emergency fund of Rs 30,000 by next March by saving Rs 4,000 a month. I will reduce rent by sharing a flat and negotiate a monthly transport pass to cut travel costs.
items.guidance: Strong answers give categories with amounts that add up to the salary, a specific saving goal with a date and a concrete way to reduce a cost.
